question.text: Per Chapter 9, private-credit yields in India tended to be high till 2023 and then moderated in 2024. The PRIMARY reason for moderation was:

answer.text: RBI imposing a ceiling on private-credit yields.
SEBI capping Cat II AIF coupon at 10%.
Entry of more AIF debt funds and other private lenders — increased supply of capital lowered the yield premium.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'In India, the yields in private credit tended to be high till 2023 when lenders were few but they moderated in 2024 with the entry of more AIF debt funds and other private lenders.' Increased supply of capital from new AIF debt funds and other private lenders moderated yields. The Trap: Options A and B invent regulatory yield caps that the workbook does not describe. Option D (Section 115UB) is a tax pass-through provision and does not affect borrower-level yields. Note: Use the workbook's stated cause — entry of more AIF debt funds and other private lenders in 2024 — without layering on portfolio-construction prescriptions that the workbook does not make.
